style.visual_cues: Authored manga illustration with subject-specific storytelling: people, animals, creatures, monsters, objects, machines, environments or abstract subjects as required by the brief. Use controlled ink line weights, selective screentones, cinematic panel composition and purposeful negative space. Choose establishing views and expressive or structural close-ups that reveal the actual subject; human faces, eyes and hands are optional, never a required template. Keep subject design, form and spatial continuity consistent. Animate motivated actions, transformations, panel reveals and camera moves with readable holds. Drawing quality must carry a still frame; generic icons, dashboard cards or a blanket dot filter are not substitutes for refined manga drawing.
style.note: The source directly names or describes this visual direction. The source reference mentions manga; some source prompts are partial.

recommended_stack.name: HyperFrames
recommended_stack.runtime: HTML composition in browser; CLI orchestration in Node.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Primary pipeline for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Visual construction and motion design remain owned by the selected style renderer and motion engine.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP
suggested_libraries.purpose: Build a paused, seekable timeline and register it with HyperFrames after construction is complete.

recommended_stack.style_application: Compose the output of the selected visual and motion layers. Supply seekable time or integrate baked assets; do not replace the style-specific rendering or motion method with framework defaults.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: Use HyperFrames by default. Fall back to Remotion only when the documented fallback condition is met, and record the reason. Do not mix framework APIs.

recommended_stack.name: SVG
recommended_stack.purpose: Draw scalable shapes, icons, strokes, clipping paths, and masks.
recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Manga according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.name: Python
recommended_stack.purpose: Preprocess assets, calculate data, and manage frame sequences in a Python process, separate from browser code.
recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Manga according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.name: Pillow
recommended_stack.purpose: Crop, resize, composite transparent images, create masks, and generate pixel textures.
recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Manga according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.name: Remotion
recommended_stack.runtime: React in browser; rendering orchestrated by Node.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Conditional fallback pipeline for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Visual construction and motion design remain owned by the selected style renderer and motion engine.

recommended_stack.name: @remotion/renderer
recommended_stack.purpose: Render compositions from Node.js only when the Remotion fallback route is selected. Do not use it as a HyperFrames renderer or browser-side encoder.

recommended_stack.name: Motion
recommended_stack.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
recommended_stack.purpose: Optional animation of DOM or SVG layers for Manga. Preserve the style-specific timing and visual cues; verify deterministic video seeking before use.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Motion is an optional layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP timeline contract. Explicitly synchronize and verify seeking; use GSAP when that integration is not established. Use motion/react only within a React component runtime.

recommended_stack.name: chroma.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally validate colors, derive controlled palette variants, interpolate colors, and check foreground/background contrast.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Start with task-provided colors and the style visual_cues. Keep a shared, deterministic palette and named color tokens. Generate gradients or interpolate colors only when the style permits them; keep limited-palette, monochrome, pixel, and print treatments discrete where required. Evaluate animated color from shared composition time. Check contrast against the actual composited background; a two-color ratio alone does not verify text over transparency, gradients, textures, or video. Pass output through the selected renderer's color API and preserve its color-space handling. Native CSS/SVG colors remain sufficient when no color processing is needed.
recommended_stack.style_application: Read palette.tokens, palette.constraints and palette.agent_instruction for Manga. Validate approved colors and assess readable existing token pairs with chroma-js. Use palette.gradient only when enabled and appropriate. Preserve task/reference colors exactly; optional suggested tokens are fallback inputs, not permission to recolor assets.

tech.implementation: Subject selection: Manga is a visual storytelling language, not a requirement for human characters. Let the brief choose people, animals, creatures, monsters, objects, machines, environments or abstract subjects; do not default to a person, human face, eye close-up or hand insert. Do not anthropomorphize objects unless the story calls for it. For animals use species-specific proportions, stance, joints, gait and surface forms; for monsters establish coherent invented anatomy and repeatable features; for objects and machines use perspective, structural joins, material response, function and mechanical articulation; for environments use spatial depth, scale, architecture or natural forms; for abstract subjects establish consistent visual rules and meaningful transformations. Apply convincing volume, clear silhouette, intentional line-weight hierarchy, purposeful ink masses, contact and perspective to every subject. Select panels and details for this story, never a mandatory portrait/eye/hand montage. Human anatomy, eyes, hands, hair and clothing examples below are conditional techniques only when the selected subject actually has those features; they never require adding a human or human features. Separate subject line art, form/material layers, environmental perspective, shadow masks, screentones, panel borders and lettering. Include hair/clothing shapes only when present. Study the reference at full resolution before building: identify contour weights, proportions, hand anatomy, hair clumps, cloth folds, spatial perspective, tone placement and panel-to-panel continuity. Use original characters and settings; do not copy reference characters, dialogue, watermarks or branding. At 1280px width use roughly 3–5px silhouette emphasis, 1–2px structural contours and 0.5–1px fine detail, scaled with delivery size; use tapered filled strokes for eyelashes and select contour accents, with clean joins instead of uniform icon outlines. Construct convincing subject volume, functional structure and contact. For subjects with those features, construct face volumes and eye placement, hands with readable gesture and joints, hair with grouped strands and directional highlights, and fabric folds rooted in tension or contact. Reserve solid ink for occlusion, deep shadows and focal accents. Clip a small number of stable screentone densities and directional hatching to form and shadow planes; retain quiet white highlights and gutters instead of dotting every surface. Keep screen-tone spacing stable during masking, scaling, and pose changes, and inspect moire at actual delivery resolution. Establish foreground/midground/background and consistent perspective; do not let construction lines show through opaque objects. Choose asymmetric panels according to narrative function, selecting wider settings, relevant structural/material details or expressive close-ups without forcing a portrait/eye/hand sequence or any repeated template. Let panels appear in deliberate reading order and hold long enough to understand; use subject-appropriate action only when supported by the beat: weight transfer, animal movement, mechanical articulation, material deformation, motivated camera motion, or blink/breath/hand action when those features exist. Avoid perpetual wobble, indiscriminate speed lines, bouncing panels or changing character identity between shots. Derive all pose and panel states from seekable composition time. Finish a representative still before adding motion: inspect silhouette at thumbnail size, anatomy and line joins at full resolution, tone clipping, gutter consistency, lettering fit and subject continuity. Do not substitute a simple eye symbol, abstract nodes or triangles for an illustrated story. Code-only drawing contract: Author every story illustration directly in editable SVG paths or deterministic Canvas drawing code, including faces, hair, hands, clothing, environments, screentones and panel masks. Do not substitute AI-generated images, raster artwork, image sprites, traced generated artwork or a finished illustration with reveal overlays. Improve the code-drawn shapes themselves: use authored Bezier contours, tapered filled strokes, grouped strand shapes, intentional shadow planes and selective procedural hatching. Simplify anatomy deliberately to a coherent graphic manga vocabulary when necessary; do not promise generated-image detail that the code cannot reproduce. Animation must control the authored drawing layers and derive all states from time. Use actual subject/story artwork; do not turn this style into a backstage director-and-crew viewer. Respect approved palette and assets; a reference accent color is not permission to expand the selected palette. SVG refinement workflow: Block subject volume, silhouette, pose or structural arrangement, contact and perspective first; face landmarks and hand gesture apply only when relevant; then refine organic contours with cubic C/S Bezier paths and aligned tangent directions at smooth joins, reserving cusp corners for intentional points and creases. Improve control handles before adding more nodes. Express pressure-like ink accents as closed tapered filled shapes, not uniformly thick strokes. When the subject has eyes, build the eye from appropriate lid, lash, iris, pupil and highlight layers and reuse consistent proportions in close-ups. For a subject with hair or hands, group hair clumps around the skull with curved strand flow and reserved highlight shapes; construct fingers as overlapping curved volumes with joints, not an angular mitten. Give opaque subject shapes real base fills before adding clipped screentones and directional hatching. Keep secondary contours and texture subordinate to silhouette and focal ink masses. Inspect and revise the unanimated SVG at thumbnail and full output sizes before layering motion. Detailed paths must serve anatomy and form; increasing path count or blanket texture is not quality. Keep character, eye, hand, clothing, tone, panel and lettering layers individually editable and deterministically seekable. Artist-construction pass: Establish subject axes, mass balance, articulation, support and contact in a temporary construction view before final contours; head axis, shoulder gesture and palm/pen contact apply only to a figure doing that action. Choose one light direction; make shadow-side crevices and foreground overlaps heavier, and allow thinner or broken contours on lit edges instead of uniformly outlining every form. When hair is present, build hair as skull volume, root flow, large overlapping clumps, smaller strands and light-consistent highlights; avoid a rigid helmet with evenly spaced white slots. If a hand uses a pen, construct a pen grip from wrist angle, palm volume, thumb mass and finger gestures, checking actual contact and occlusion. Review the still with tone hidden, in an ink-only view, at full size, at thumbnail size and temporarily mirrored; correct eye alignment, jaw shape, silhouette and accidental tangencies before adding texture. Tone must follow surface and light, not decorate every region. Assess anatomy, expression and focal hierarchy by inspecting the rendered still; valid XML, extra paths, a longer SVG budget and passing technical tests do not prove drawing quality. Only then add deterministic movement. These construction and inking rules apply to any subject in this style; do not impose the sample character or composition. Character-quality construction (only for a subject with relevant head/face/body features, never a requirement to add them): Choose head yaw, pitch, tilt, gaze and emotion before final paths. Block skull volume, jaw planes, face centreline and a curved feature line; a 2D rotation is not a three-quarter head turn. Place eyes, brows, nose, mouth and ears on those forms using proportions appropriate to the intended character. A far eye must be angle-aware, narrower and nearer the nose where perspective requires; do not mirror identical front-facing eye symbols to represent a turned head. Keep eyelids wrapped around eye volume, with gaze shared by both eyes. Coordinate lid opening, brows and mouth to communicate the intended emotion rather than adding highlights for decoration. Establish a line of action and shoulder/torso relationship, and connect the neck to jaw and shoulders plausibly; avoid a static frontal mannequin when the story needs character acting. Build hair volume over the skull with overlapping clumps and root direction, not a black helmet hiding weak construction. Review an ink-only character with tone and highlights hidden: pose, head angle, gaze, expression, silhouette, near/far feature placement and hand-to-prop contact must read before detail. Compare full-size, thumbnail and mirrored views; correct structure before adding texture. Reuse design proportions across shots while authoring angle-specific contours. Maintain code-only editable drawing and derive movement from deterministic time. Eye-integrity pass (only when the chosen subject has visible eyes): Construct the pair on one head-volume and feature-line model with one shared gaze target; project each eye and iris for that view rather than independently nudging pupils by arbitrary pixels. Perspective can narrow the far eye without accidentally changing its lid opening or expression into a squint. Author the eye opening, sclera, lid contour and its clip path from matching landmarks in the same local coordinate space; changing an opening requires changing its mask and lid together. Keep iris and pupil clipped inside the eye opening, nest highlights inside the iris, and draw upper lids/occluding features above them. Check the visible iris against both lids at neutral and extreme gaze positions; avoid detached pupils, inconsistent occlusion and collapsed dark blobs. At preview-card scale simplify iris texture and catchlights before enlarging or distorting anatomy; fine screentone and multiple tiny highlights are optional. During gaze motion move the iris/pupil/highlight assembly together inside the lid mask; during a blink change the opening/occlusion coherently rather than scaling a complete eye symbol. Before animation, inspect an eye-pair crop and the whole head in a neutral pose at full size and actual card size. Then inspect gaze extremes, blink keyframes and the settled expression, including direct/backward seeks. Fix perspective, shared gaze, expression, clipping and small-scale readability before publishing; valid SVG or general render checks alone do not pass this eye review. Do not add eyes to subjects that do not need them.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Manga without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider bounded pupil following with optional delayed brows, slight head tilt, and scheduled blinks. Require suitable facial layers or a rig, preserve expression and drawing cadence, and do not interpret this as viewer eye tracking.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

Use a cinematic opening with separately animated illustrated objects, speed-line accents and expressive motion text. Stage the action across panels and end in the approved composition. Prefer this over pupil-only movement or tiny ambient wiggles.

Limited-color lettering can replace phrases with reading holds and controlled glyph poses. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

A monochrome punctuation crop can connect authored panels without screen-tone distortion. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers. For an opening or gallery demo, prefer motion-016 when separable illustration and text layers exist; animate both focal objects and meaningful lettering.

constraints: These hex values are authored suggestions, not previously supplied exact colors or canonical style definitions.

Candidate opaque text pairing; verify final size and compositing.

palette.composition_guidance: Use one dominant background and a clear foreground hierarchy. Keep accents subordinate except where the style calls for bold geometric fields. Preserve exact anchors; improve balance through area, spacing and placement rather than hue substitution. Gradient samples and material lighting are not extra base-color licenses.
palette.agent_instruction: Resolve colors in this order: task-provided exact palette, established brand or approved source palette, existing semantic color mappings, then this optional example. Read visual_cues and palette.constraints. Preserve approved anchor values, color families, ink counts and asset colors. Use chroma-js for validation, equivalent normalization and contrast assessment; evaluate gradients only when enabled and appropriate. Select readable token pairs from contrast_checks, otherwise move text onto an existing contrasting backing. Record the resolved tokens and inspect actual composited frames before rendering.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of Manga, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

suggested_combinations.selection_guidance: Manga is strongest alone in strict black-and-white with stable screentone. Use a hybrid only for depth in key close-ups or for instructional annotation.

supporting_styles.role: Spatial layering: separates line art, screentone and background into parallax planes for selected close-ups

suggestions.rationale: Gentle parallax adds cinematic depth to panel reveals while the ink and tone layers remain flat drawings.
suggestions.best_for: Story trailers, dramatic reveal moments, webtoon-style promos.
suggestions.video_application: Only hero panels split into 2–3 planes with slow push-ins; other panels use standard panel reveals.
suggestions.html_application: Panels gain subtle pointer/scroll parallax via SVG layers, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion and on small screens.
consistency_rules: Screentone scale never changes with plane depth.

supporting_styles.role: Margin annotations and callouts for teaching or commentary

suggestions.best_for: Educational manga, onboarding guides, process explainers.

productionPolicy.principle: Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique.
productionPolicy.style_renderer: Owns visual construction: drawing, geometry, materials, lighting, typography, masks, textures, and specialist asset generation. Use the style-specific recommended technologies and implementation guidance.
productionPolicy.motion_engine: Owns trajectories, transforms, easing, transitions, deformation, and simulation. Select engines or algorithms appropriate to the action, with one owner for each animated property.
productionPolicy.render_pipeline: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.
productionPolicy.integration: Visual and motion layers expose deterministic state at composition time, or supply baked assets or frame sequences. The pipeline supplies seekable time and composes their output. Timeline registration and frame hooks are integration adapters, not substitutes for style-specific rendering or motion.
productionPolicy.selection: Choose only needed stack entries. A technology may serve multiple roles, but document its actual responsibility. Optional authoring, interaction, color, and preprocessing tools are not mandatory renderers or motion engines.

motionReferences.name: Cursor-Driven Gaze Tracking
motionReferences.description: A character follows a pointer with pupil motion constrained to its eye sockets. Brows can follow with a short delay, the head can tilt subtly, and periodic blinks add secondary expression. Eye direction remains coordinated; this is illustrated character animation, not measurement of the viewer's gaze.
motion_sequence: Establish a neutral character face and bounded eye sockets.
Move the target and shift the pupils within their sockets; add delayed brow movement and a slight head tilt when the assets support them.
Include scheduled blinks and hold readable reactions, returning to a neutral pose when the designed interaction ends.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Author the target path and any visible cursor on the composition timeline. Evaluate gaze directly from target position at each time. Model any delay analytically from the authored path or bake it; do not rely on a live smoothing loop or webcam input.

suggested_libraries.name: Three.js

suggested_libraries.name: PixiJS

suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use a private ticker and disable autoplay with autoStart: false and sharedTicker: false; stop any already-started application. suggested_libraries.name: Motion
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional DOM or SVG implementation of Cursor-Driven Gaze Tracking using controlled keyframes or sequences. Verify synchronization with the selected video framework before adopting this route.

suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Pause playback and set animation.time in seconds from composition time, then verify that forward, backward, and direct seeks update the visible result. Motion is an optional animation layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP registration contract; keep the registered GSAP timeline as the framework clock and explicitly synchronize Motion. Use motion/react only within mounted React components.

tech.implementation: Use SVG or DOM pupil groups clipped within eye shapes, or existing 3D eye and head rigs. Bound the displacement or rotation and retain coordinated gaze. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motionReferences.name: Scroll-Driven Chaptered Scene Transition
motionReferences.description: Scroll progress coordinates a handoff between narrative chapters. An outgoing scene yields to an incoming scene through a chosen fade, wipe, panel rotation, or shared-element move; text and media states change with the same progress. Clear start and end states preserve reading order in both scroll directions.
motion_sequence: Establish the outgoing chapter and a readable closing state.
Across a defined progress window, coordinate outgoing and incoming scene states with one selected transition treatment and synchronized copy.
Resolve the incoming chapter into its readable state before beginning the next handoff; reversing progress retraces the same transition.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Schedule chapter windows and transition intervals on composition time. Explicitly choose the handoff type. If the style requires a continuous shot, use a coherent camera or spatial handoff instead of an incompatible cut.

motionReferences.name: Cinematic Manga Opening Sequence
motionReferences.description: A manga-inspired opening that animates separate illustrated subjects, speed lines and expressive lettering in coordinated narrative beats. Panels stay anchored while focal objects enter, action accents build and text punches in. This is an authored creative recipe, not a reproduction of a particular film opening.
motion_sequence: Establish the page composition and panel frames; separate coherent subject, accent and text layers while preserving authored transforms.
Reveal or draw the main subject, then introduce secondary objects with staggered entrances; use speed-line sweeps and bounded impact pops to build energy.
Punch in expressive sound-effect or title lettering on the action beat. Introduce dialogue or concluding copy after the subject is readable.
Settle all layers into the approved illustration and hold a readable ending. For a looping gallery study, restart at a clear editorial cut rather than imperceptible breathing.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Author timed beats for a three-second gallery study or expand them into a full opening. Maintain a perceptible change at thumbnail size and readable final copy. Do not merely wobble the whole page or track a pupil.

Await export and split layers deliberately when separate animation is required; a flattened image does not preserve editable shapes. Animate those assets in the chosen framework. Verify signatures against the installed SDK; tldraw is not a video renderer or an automatic timeline adapter.

tech.implementation: Construct distinct SVG groups or PixiJS containers for subjects, panels, speed lines and expressive text. Animate neutral wrappers or containers with a paused GSAP timeline; preserve original authored transforms. Use stroke dash drawing only on visible unfilled paths; use reveal masks or opacity/scale entrances for filled artwork. Text has its own timed punch-in and final reading hold. Keep every layer seekable from composition time.
tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

motionReferences.executable_prompt_template: Build a Cinematic Manga Opening Sequence for {{subject}} in {{visual_style}}. Inspect the approved illustration and separate meaningful subject, speed-line, panel and expressive-text layers. Resolve {{motion_parameters}} into distinct entrances, optional stroke drawing, bounded impact pops and text punch-ins; preserve exact palette anchors and authored geometry. Do not animate every primitive independently. Make the action readable at thumbnail size and end with readable copy. Select SVG/Canvas/PixiJS for illustration and GSAP or Anime.js for seekable layer motion as appropriate. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for composition, synchronization, validation and export; HyperFrames is first choice and Remotion is the conditional fallback. Suggest audio based on the topic, with silent gallery output. Validate direct seeks and visible frame changes. Optional variant: Add optional compact illustrated-intro variants: title scale punch and settle; radial/face accents; lineup/caption handoff; overview-to-panel zoom. Preserve illustrated staging and reading holds; do not impose manga marks on unrelated media.

interaction.progress_driver: A single seekable composition timeline schedules independent layers; live scroll or pointer input is unnecessary.
interaction.exit_behavior: Pause or seek without losing layer state; preserve a reduced-motion illustrated alternative.

motionReferences.audio_direction_prompt: Based on the topic and audience, suggest instrumental pacing, short impact accents, page or ink sounds, and whether narration or vocals help. Keep gallery demos silent; avoid prescribing a fixed genre.
verification: Check significant frame changes at 320×180, not only a running timeline.
Check subjects, action accents and text each contribute to the staged narrative.
Inspect panel boundaries, connections, palette, and reading holds.
Verify start, intermediate and final seeks match sequential playback.
motionReferences.adaptation_guidance: Use strong staged entrances for Manga and Comic Book Art; adjust cadence and intensity to the subject. Keep backgrounds and reading anchors fixed. Use masks or authentic layer geometry for wipes instead of pretending a flat image has a 3D camera. Preserve illustrated staging and reading holds; do not impose manga marks on unrelated media.

motionReferences.name: Radial Logo Burst
motionReferences.description: Stage a central mark, repeated outward white circular waves at a deliberate pulse tempo, coordinated rays and a compact party-popper burst of white and dark squares, triangles, circles and crosses. Keep tumbling confetti close around the icon; a strong sudden forward impulse toward the viewer slows into a very brief airborne hang, then a natural gravity-driven fall, never a canvas-wide distribution. Use an expanding circular mask for palette inversion while retaining the mark center. Let the burst decay into a stable logo hold; keep later particles subordinate. Use the icon center as the popper exit: pieces begin tiny at that point, shoot forward toward the viewer with a small spread around the center, never an upward launch, increase in apparent size, overlap in front of the icon, briefly hang and then fall. Keep the burst compact; express depth with coherent perspective scale and layer ordering.
motion_sequence: Establish one centered approved mark and its initial field.

Release successive soft circular waves from the fixed mark center at regular beat intervals. Emit a compact cluster of varied white and dark confetti shapes around the icon: a powerful quick forward launch toward the viewer, rotation and tumbling, a very short airborne hang, then a natural accelerating downward fall. Keep confetti local to the icon even as waves expand beyond it. Use the icon center as the popper exit: pieces begin tiny at that point, shoot forward toward the viewer with a small spread around the center, never an upward launch, increase in apparent size, overlap in front of the icon, briefly hang and then fall. Keep the burst compact; express depth with coherent perspective scale and layer ordering.
Expand a circular mask to invert the field and mark palette, then let accents decay into a stable identity hold.
